meeting.title: Foundry Agent Customer Workshop
meeting.objective: Confirm the customer demo path, presentation quality requirements, and follow-up ownership.

transcript.speaker: Taylor
transcript.text: We need a browser-based meeting workflow rather than asking users to run Python commands.

transcript.speaker: Avery
transcript.text: The local Web UI will call Azure OpenAI through the Responses API and keep the Outlook handoff on the Windows device.

transcript.speaker: Morgan
transcript.text: The model output must stay grounded in finalized transcript evidence and must not invent owners, dates, or product commitments.

transcript.speaker: Taylor
transcript.text: The generated PowerPoint needs a reusable visual template, stronger hierarchy, and an editable action register.

transcript.speaker: Jordan
transcript.text: The mind map should be easy to scan, with short branches for topics, decisions, actions, risks, and open questions.

transcript.speaker: Avery
transcript.text: We agreed to use GPT-5.4 with medium reasoning effort for the meeting analysis.

transcript.speaker: Morgan
transcript.text: Avery will prepare the engineering template and demo package before Friday.

transcript.speaker: Jordan
transcript.text: Jordan will validate the PowerPoint and Mermaid mind-map rendering with two materially different meetings.

transcript.speaker: Taylor
transcript.text: Can the customer replace the default slide colors and logo without changing the generation code?

transcript.speaker: Avery
transcript.text: The email output will remain an unsent New Outlook draft with the mind map and PowerPoint attached for human review.

visual_context.description: The shared architecture diagram shows: Windows Web UI, local BFF, Azure OpenAI Responses API, artifact generation, and New Outlook draft review.
The design review lists a six-slide narrative: cover, executive summary, topics, decisions and actions, mind map, and open questions.
